findings.title: Client-side upload size limit hardcoded to 10 MB
findings.body: The validation now uses a fixed `10 * 1024` KB instead of `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. This ignores the configured maximum for both images and attachments: attachments larger than the site limit can be selected/uploaded, and images may be blocked even if the configured image limit is larger than 10 MB. It also makes client-side enforcement inconsistent with the server-side behavior introduced in this PR.

findings.title: 413 error message uses hardcoded 10 MB limit
findings.body: On HTTP 413 the code reports `max_size_kb: 10 * 1024` instead of the relevant site setting. Users can be told the limit is 10 MB even when the configured maximum image or attachment size is different, so the error message no longer reflects the actual upload policy.

findings.title: URL uploads are downloaded with a fixed 10 MB limit
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` limit and is used before knowing whether the URL is an image. API URL uploads can now fetch up to 10 MB even when the configured maximum is lower, and non-image/attachment URL uploads are not subject to the attachment limit. This can bypass site limits and waste bandwidth or memory.

findings.title: Downsizing overwrites the input tempfile in place
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` uses the same path as input and output. ImageMagick/gifsicle are not guaranteed to safely overwrite the file they are reading, and in-place rewriting can truncate or corrupt the original upload if the tool opens the output for writing before fully reading the input or if the operation fails. A temporary output file should be created and atomically replace the original only on success.

findings.title: Failed or ineffective downsizing is ignored
findings.body: The loop does not check the boolean returned by `OptimizedImage.downsize` and does not abort if the file is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` after five attempts. If conversion fails, the code will retry pointlessly and then continue to `Upload.create_for` with an unchanged or corrupted file, possibly storing an invalid or oversized upload or returning a confusing error.

findings.title: Tempfile path lacks original extension, breaking animation/format detection
findings.body: The automatic downsize passes `tempfile.path` to `OptimizedImage.optimize`, which only uses the animated code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. Rack/Tempfile paths for uploads usually do not carry the original filename extension, so GIFs will not be detected as animated and will be processed by ImageMagick with `[0]`, stripping animation even when `allow_animation` is enabled. The missing extension can also make ImageMagick choose the wrong output format. Use a temp file with the original extension or pass the desired format explicitly.

findings.title: SVG/vector images are downsized like raster images
findings.body: The condition treats any filename matching `FileHelper.is_image?` as resizable, which includes SVG in Discourse. Unlike `OptimizedImage.create_for`, this code has no special case for `.svg`; calling ImageMagick `convert` on an SVG to reduce file size can rasterize or otherwise alter the vector file, or fail. Large SVG uploads can therefore be corrupted or lose their original content.

findings.title: Duplicate `downsize` definition overwrites the four-argument method
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by arity. The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the preceding four-argument `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. The four-argument version is dead code, and any existing caller using width/height will have `height` interpreted as `opts`, likely causing errors or malformed ImageMagick dimensions. If both signatures are needed, use distinct method names or a single method that normalizes arguments.

findings.title: No tests for automatic downsizing and changed upload limits
findings.body: The PR introduces server-side image downsizing, changes URL download limits, and alters client-side upload validation, but no test files are added or updated. Without coverage for oversized images, failed conversions, SVG/GIF handling, and attachment limits, regressions in these upload paths are likely.
